threads.thread_goal: Align on current-state workflows and confirm scope for standardisation

messages.text: Hi team, thanks for joining this project. We're kicking off the standardisation of patient intake and admin workflows across our units. To get started, I'd like everyone to share how intake and admin tasks currently run in their areas. This will help us map the current state (A1) and identify where we have variations. Can each of you walk through your unit's process—registration, consent, documentation, handoffs? Let's aim to capture this over the next few days so we can move into T1 mapping.

Thanks for the clear kickoff. In our unit, we start with patient registration at the front desk—name, DOB, contact details. Then the healthcare assistant does a quick ID check and hands over a consent form. The nurse reviews it before the patient sees the clinician. We've had some issues with forms getting lost between handoffs, and sometimes patients aren't clear on what they're consenting to. I can document this in detail by end of week.

Our process is a bit different. We do registration and consent together—the admin staff walks the patient through the form while they're filling it out. It's slower but we get fewer consent issues. However, we're not always consistent about which fields are mandatory. I'll document what we do, but I'm wondering if we should be looking at all three units or just the main ones for this first wave?

Good question. I think we should focus on the three main units first—that's where most of the patient volume is. We can add the smaller units later if needed. For our unit, intake is fairly straightforward: registration, basic health questions, consent, then handoff to nursing. But we do have some older adults who need extra time and support with forms. I'll get the details documented.

I can help with documenting our unit's process. We have a mix of disability support and older adult cases, so intake varies quite a bit depending on the patient type. Sometimes we need a carer or family member involved in consent, which adds complexity. I'll pull together what we do, though I may need some guidance on how detailed the documentation should be.

I'll contribute what I can from our area. We follow the clinical guidelines pretty closely, but I'm not sure how much detail you need for the mapping. Should we include every single step, or just the main ones? Also, are we looking at intake for all patient types or focusing on specific scenarios?

Great input. Let me clarify scope: we'll focus on the three main units for this first wave (D1 candidate). For detail level (D2 candidate), I'd suggest we capture the main steps, key handoffs, and pain points—not every micro-step, but enough to understand where variations exist and where errors happen. For patient types, let's cover adult, older adult, and disability support cases since those are our main scenarios. Does that work for everyone?

That scope makes sense. I'll document our process with those three patient types in mind and highlight where we see the most friction. Should we also note which steps are currently working well, or just focus on the problems?

Good thinking—yes, please note what's working too. That helps us keep the good parts and only change what needs fixing. Let's aim to have all three unit maps in by end of week so we can consolidate into A1 and start drafting the standard SOP. I'll set up a shared doc for everyone to add their workflows.

I'll get our unit's map done by Friday. One thing I'm thinking about—we have some older adults who come in with carers, and the consent process gets complicated. Should we be documenting that as a separate scenario or part of the older adult intake?

Document it as part of the older adult scenario but flag it as a variation. That way we can see how often it happens and whether the standard SOP needs a specific branch for carer involvement. Good catch.
I'll have our documentation ready by Friday as well. We do have quite a few disability support cases where consent is complex, so I'll make sure to capture those variations clearly.
Will do. I'll document our process and include notes on where we see delays or confusion. Looking forward to seeing how the three units compare.
I'll contribute our unit's map by Friday. Just to confirm—should we include the time it takes for each step, or just the sequence?
Good question. Include rough timing if you have it—that helps us spot where delays are happening. But don't spend time measuring precisely; ballpark is fine.

I've started pulling together our workflow doc. One thing I want to flag early: we have some inconsistency in how we handle consent for patients with cognitive concerns. Some staff ask the patient directly, others involve family first. Should that be part of the standard SOP or handled separately?

That's exactly the kind of variation we need to capture in A1. Document how you currently handle it, and we'll address it in the standard SOP (T2) once we see all three units' approaches. This is important for compliance, so we'll want to get it right.
Agreed. I think once we see all the variations, it'll be clearer what needs to be standardised and what needs flexibility. Looking forward to consolidating everything.

Perfect. So to confirm our decisions: we're focusing on the three main units (D1), and we'll capture main steps, handoffs, pain points, and timing at a ballpark level (D2). All maps due by end of week. Once I consolidate A1, we'll move into drafting the standard SOP and forms. Thanks everyone for the clarity.
Thanks for the clear direction. I'll get our unit's map done by Friday.
Got it. I'll have our documentation ready.
Will do. See you next week with the consolidated maps.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise the draft standard intake SOP and forms

messages.text: Hi team, I've consolidated the workflow maps from all three units into A1, and I can see some clear patterns and variations. Based on that, I've drafted a standard patient intake SOP (A2, T2) and a set of unified intake and consent form templates (A3, T3). I'm posting both for async review and comments. Please take a look and flag any concerns, especially around compliance, clarity, and whether the steps match what you actually do. I'd like to lock these in by mid-week so we can move into training prep.

I've reviewed the draft SOP and forms. The core steps look solid—registration, ID check, consent, documentation. One thing I'd suggest: the consent section should explicitly mention what to do if a patient lacks capacity or needs a carer's input. Right now it's a bit vague. Also, the form templates are clear, but I'd recommend adding a field for 'consent given by' (patient, carer, legal representative) so we're explicit about who's authorising.

Excellent points. Those are exactly the kinds of clarifications we need for compliance. I'll add a decision tree for capacity assessment and a 'consent given by' field to the forms. That should cover the variations we saw in the unit maps.

I've looked at the SOP. It's pretty comprehensive. One question: the form has a section for 'basic health information'—how much detail should we capture there? In our unit, we ask about allergies, current medications, and mobility needs. Is that the right level?
That's the right level for intake. Allergies, meds, and mobility are critical for safety and handoff to the clinician. I'll make sure the form template includes those fields explicitly. Good catch.

I've reviewed the SOP and forms. They look reasonable. One thing I'm wondering about: the SOP says the healthcare assistant does the initial intake, but in our unit, sometimes the admin staff does it. Should we be clearer about who does what, or is it flexible?

Good question. The SOP should be clear about roles. Let me revise: admin staff handle registration and initial data capture; healthcare assistants do the ID check and consent review; nurses sign off before the patient sees the clinician. That way we're explicit about who's responsible for each step. Does that match what you're doing?
Yes, that matches our process. Clear roles will help avoid confusion.

I've looked at the draft. The forms are pretty clear, but I'm concerned about the disability support section. We have patients with various disabilities, and the form might not capture all the relevant information. Should we have a separate form for disability cases, or add more fields to the main form?

That's a fair concern. Rather than separate forms, let's add a 'disability and support needs' section to the main form with checkboxes for common scenarios (mobility, communication, cognitive, sensory). That way we have one form but it's flexible enough for different needs. I'll revise and share an updated version by tomorrow.

I've reviewed the SOP. It's well-structured. One thing I'd flag: the documentation step mentions 'record in patient file,' but we need to be clear about data protection and confidentiality. Should we add a note about secure handling and who has access?

Absolutely right. Data protection is critical. I'll add a section to the SOP on secure handling, access controls, and confidentiality obligations. That's something we'll also want the quality and compliance officer to review before we finalise.
Good point about compliance review. Should we schedule a formal review with the quality and compliance officer before we lock in the SOP and forms, or do you want to do a first pass with us first?

Let's do a first pass with the team to get the core content right, then I'll send to the quality and compliance officer for formal review. That way we're not wasting their time on drafts that still have issues. I'll incorporate everyone's feedback by tomorrow and post a revised version.
Sounds good. I'll review the revised version once you post it.
Will do. Looking forward to seeing the updated forms with the disability section.

I've updated A2 and A3 based on your feedback. Key changes: clearer roles and responsibilities, capacity assessment decision tree, 'consent given by' field, disability and support needs section, and data protection notes. I've also added explicit fields for allergies, medications, and mobility. Please take another look and let me know if these address your concerns. Once you confirm, I'll send to the quality and compliance officer for formal review.
Much better. The capacity assessment tree is clear, and the 'consent given by' field is exactly what we need. I'm satisfied with these versions.
Looks good. The role clarity is helpful, and the disability section covers what we need.
I'm happy with the updates. The forms now capture the key information we need, and the SOP is clear about who does what.
The disability section is much better now. I think this will work well for our cases.
The data protection notes are good. I think this is ready for compliance review.

Great. I'm hearing consensus that A2 and A3 are ready for compliance review (D3 and D4 approved). I'll send these to the quality and compliance officer today and aim to get their feedback by end of week. Once they sign off, we can move into training prep. Thanks everyone for the thorough review.

threads.thread_goal: Lock training approach, materials, and schedule for the pilot

messages.text: Hi team, the quality and compliance officer has approved A2 and A3, so we're ready to move into training. I've drafted a training deck (A5) and a quick-reference checklist for healthcare assistants (A4). I've also sketched out a proposed training calendar (T5) that fits around shift patterns. Please review the materials and the schedule, and let me know if the format works for your units. I'm aiming to lock this in by mid-week so we can start scheduling sessions.

I've reviewed the training deck and checklist. The deck is comprehensive and covers the key points well. The checklist is clear and fits on one page, which is good. One suggestion: the checklist could include a quick reference for the capacity assessment decision tree from the SOP. That's a critical step and staff might need a visual reminder.
Good idea. I'll add a mini decision tree to the checklist. That way staff have a quick visual guide without needing to flip back to the full SOP.

I've looked at the training calendar. The proposed times work for our unit, but I'd suggest adding an evening session for staff who work later shifts. Also, will there be async materials for people who can't make the live sessions?

Good points. I'll add an evening session to the calendar, and yes, I'm planning to record the live sessions and create a short async video summary plus a written FAQ. That way everyone has options. I'll update T5 with those additions.

The training materials look good. I'm wondering about the format—is this a presentation-style training, or more interactive? Our staff respond better to interactive sessions where they can ask questions and work through scenarios.

Great question. I'm planning for interactive sessions—I'll present the key points, but then we'll work through some scenarios together (e.g., 'patient with cognitive concerns,' 'carer involved in consent'). That way staff get practice with the new process before the pilot starts. Does that work?

I've reviewed the materials. The checklist is helpful, but I'm not sure it covers all the disability support scenarios we discussed. Should we add a section for common disability-related questions or variations?
Good catch. I'll add a 'disability support considerations' section to the checklist with common scenarios and how to handle them. That way staff have a quick reference for those cases.
I've looked at the training calendar. The times work for our unit. One question: how long are the live sessions, and will there be a Q&A at the end?
Sessions will be about 60 minutes: 30 minutes for content and scenarios, 30 minutes for Q&A and discussion. That way we cover the material but leave plenty of time for questions.
That timing works well. I think the training approach is solid—interactive sessions with scenarios, plus async materials for flexibility. I'm ready to move forward with this.

I've updated A4 and A5 based on your feedback: added the capacity assessment decision tree to the checklist, disability support considerations section, and updated T5 with evening sessions and async materials. I'm also planning for interactive scenario-based training with 60-minute sessions. Does this approach work for everyone (D5)?
Yes, this works for us. The interactive format will help staff feel more confident with the new process.
Looks good. The disability section will be helpful for our staff.
Perfect. The interactive approach is exactly what we need. I'm confident staff will engage well with this.
This works for us. The timing and format are good.

Excellent. Now let's confirm the training schedule (D6). I'm proposing: two live sessions per unit (morning and evening), plus recorded async materials available by the start of the pilot. Target attendance is at least 80% of staff in the pilot unit. Does this work, and which unit should we pilot in?
I think our unit is a good candidate for the pilot. We have good engagement from staff, and we're ready to try the new process. I can help coordinate the training schedule with our team.

Great. Let's use your unit for the pilot. I'll schedule the two live sessions for next week—one morning, one evening—and have the async materials ready by the end of the week. Can you help with attendance tracking and getting the team to commit to at least one session?
Absolutely. I'll send out the training calendar to our team and track attendance. I'm confident we'll hit the 80% target.

Perfect. So to confirm: we're using your unit for the pilot, training format is interactive with scenarios, two live sessions next week plus async materials, target 80% attendance (D6 confirmed). I'll finalize the training schedule and materials by end of week. T4 and T5 are on track.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate the pilot run and daily issue handling

messages.text: Hi team, the training is complete and we're ready to start the pilot. The pilot will run for two weeks in the unit led by 529990, starting Monday. During the pilot, we'll track errors, delays, and staff feedback using A6. I'll do daily check-ins with the unit contact to catch any issues early. The goal is to see how the new workflow performs in a real environment and identify any adjustments needed before full rollout. Let's confirm the exact dates and expectations (D7).

Confirmed. We're ready to start Monday. I've briefed the team on the new workflow, and they're prepared. I'll be the main contact for daily check-ins. We'll track any issues and feedback as they come up.

Perfect. So pilot dates are Monday through Friday of next week, then the following week (two weeks total). I'll check in with you daily at 4 PM to see how things are going. Please flag any blockers, errors, or staff concerns immediately so we can adjust quickly. Does that work?
Yes, 4 PM daily check-in works. I'll have updates ready for you.

Great. I'm also setting up A6 to track metrics. We'll capture: number of intake errors (missing fields, consent issues, ID problems), average time per intake, and staff feedback. I'll share the tracking sheet with you so you can log issues as they happen.
Good. I'll make sure the team logs issues in A6 as they occur. That way we have real-time data.

Excellent. One more thing: if there's a critical incident linked to the new workflow, please flag it immediately. We want to catch any safety issues right away. Otherwise, we'll review all the data at the end of the two weeks and prepare the pilot report (A7).
Understood. I'll escalate any critical issues immediately. Otherwise, we'll track everything in A6 and review at the end.

Perfect. So to confirm: pilot runs Monday through two weeks, daily 4 PM check-ins, real-time issue logging in A6, immediate escalation of critical incidents (D7 confirmed). Let's make this work. I'll send out the tracking sheet today.
Good luck with the pilot. Let us know if you need any support from the other units.
Yes, we're here if you need anything. Looking forward to seeing how it goes.
Good luck. We'll be ready to learn from the pilot results.
All set. Let's see how the new workflow performs.
Thanks everyone. I'll keep you posted on progress. First check-in tomorrow at 4 PM.
Day 1 update: Pilot started smoothly. Staff are following the new intake process. A few questions about the consent form, but nothing blocking. I'll have more details at the 4 PM check-in.
Great to hear. Looking forward to the check-in. Keep logging issues in A6 as they come up.

Will do. Day 2 update: Intake times are slightly longer than before, but staff are getting faster. No errors so far. One staff member asked about the capacity assessment decision tree—I clarified it and they're good now.
Good. The slight increase in time is expected as staff get used to the new process. Once they're comfortable, it should normalize. Keep tracking in A6.

Day 3 update: Intake times are normalizing. Staff are more confident with the process. One patient had a carer involved in consent, and the team handled it well using the decision tree. No errors logged.
Excellent. That's exactly what we want to see—staff confident and handling complex scenarios correctly. Keep it up.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on adjustments and rollout plan

messages.text: Hi team, the pilot is complete. I've compiled the results into A7 (pilot evaluation report). Key findings: intake errors decreased by 40% compared to baseline, average intake time increased by 8% initially but normalized by day 5, staff feedback was positive overall, and the new workflow handled complex scenarios (carer involvement, capacity assessment) well. There are a few minor adjustments recommended in the report. Please review A7 and let me know your thoughts. Once we align on adjustments, we'll finalize the SOP and forms (A2, A3) and prepare the full rollout plan (T10).

Great results. I've reviewed A7. The 40% error reduction is significant. The minor adjustments look reasonable—mainly clarifications on the consent form and a note about timing expectations for staff. I'm ready to move forward with these changes.
Good. The adjustments are minor and should be quick to implement. I'll update A2 and A3 with the clarifications and have them ready for final review by tomorrow.
I've reviewed A7. The results are encouraging. The error reduction is significant, and the feedback from the pilot unit is positive. I'm satisfied with the adjustments proposed.
I've looked at A7. The pilot results are solid. The adjustments make sense. I'm ready to move forward with the rollout.
Good results from the pilot. The error reduction is impressive. I'm happy with the proposed adjustments.
I've reviewed A7. The pilot results are positive. The adjustments are reasonable. I'm ready to proceed with the rollout plan.

I've updated A2 and A3 with the minor adjustments from the pilot. I've also prepared a change log (T9) documenting all the adjustments and rationale. Now I need to prepare the full rollout implementation plan (T10). This should include: rollout phases for all units, timeline, owners, risks, and mitigation actions. I'll draft this by tomorrow and share for review.
Good. I'm ready to review the rollout plan. I'd suggest we phase it by unit—start with the two units that are ready, then the third unit. That way we can learn from each phase.

Good thinking. I'll structure the rollout in three phases: Phase 1 (two units), Phase 2 (third unit), with two weeks between phases for stabilization. I'll also include a communication plan (T11) and post-rollout monitoring guide (A8, T12). Let me draft all of this and share by tomorrow.
The phased approach makes sense. It gives us time to stabilize each phase before moving to the next. I'm ready to review the full plan.

I've prepared the full rollout implementation plan (T10), communication pack (T11), and post-rollout monitoring guide (A8, T12). The plan includes: Phase 1 (two units, weeks 1-2), Phase 2 (third unit, weeks 3-4), with clear owners, timelines, and risk mitigation. The communication pack has an announcement and FAQ. The monitoring guide defines how we'll track metrics post-rollout. Please review and let me know if you have concerns.
I've reviewed the rollout plan. The phasing is good, and the communication pack is clear. The monitoring guide is comprehensive. I'm satisfied with this approach.
The rollout plan looks solid. The phasing gives us time to stabilize, and the communication is clear. I'm ready to move forward.
The plan is comprehensive. I'm satisfied with the approach.
Good plan. The phasing and communication are clear. I'm ready to proceed.
The rollout plan is well-structured. The monitoring guide is helpful. I'm satisfied with this approach.

Excellent. I'm hearing consensus on the rollout plan, adjusted SOP and forms, and monitoring approach. Let me confirm the final decision (D8): we approve the final adjusted SOP and forms (A2, A3), the full rollout implementation plan (T10), the communication pack (T11), and the post-rollout monitoring guide (A8, T12). Are we ready to move forward with rollout?
Yes, I'm ready. Let's move forward with the rollout.
Ready to proceed. Let's get this rolled out.
Yes, let's move forward.
Ready to go. Let's start the rollout.
Yes, I'm ready. Let's proceed with the rollout.

Perfect. D8 is confirmed. We're approved to move forward with the full rollout. I'll send out the communication pack (T11) today and schedule Phase 1 training for next week. Phase 1 units, please confirm your readiness. We're on track to complete the full rollout within the project timeline.
